candidate_diagrams.claim: An embedded finite plane multigraph has polygon faces; the outer boundary follows unbounded-region incidences in plane cyclic order; bridges may be traversed twice; Cayley labels satisfy g(w)=g(v)x.
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The definition depends on planar incidence, edge germs, face attachment and a fixed outer-walk direction; a small labeled embedded example would clarify how a bridge is read twice and how the left-face convention fixes orientation.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: One face bounded by a cyclically labeled polygon; one thin bridge attached at a cut vertex and traversed out and back by the outer walk; arrows on oriented edges with inverse labels on reversal; show unbounded region on the left of the directed outer walk. Avoid suggesting all singular diagrams have this shape.
candidate_diagrams.confidence: possible, source-supported; not required for the definition

candidate_diagrams.claim: A group acting without inversions on a tree is identified with the fundamental group of its quotient graph of groups, and the associated Bass–Serre coset tree is equivariantly isomorphic to the original tree.
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The statement identifies an action tree with a coset tree built from stabilizers, edge groups and boundary maps; this is a genuine map and incidence relationship with choices of lifts and a maximal subtree.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: A minimal illustrative tree with G-action, quotient graph and selected maximal subtree; label vertex/edge stabilizers and boundary monomorphisms, chosen lifts/connecting elements; show the associated coset vertices γG_v and edges γG_e mapping equivariantly to translates in T. Make this an example diagram, not an asserted general finite quotient.

candidate_diagrams.claim: A finite triangulated disk maps affinely to R²; successive boundary arcs map to axes and an outer L-shaped region, signed ray crossings count image coverage, and internal edge contributions cancel.
candidate_diagrams.kind: oriented planar map / signed crossing diagram
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The proof depends on orientation signs, the boundary arc order, a generic ray, and cancellation across internal edges; these are easy to misread from prose alone.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: Show a disk triangulation with coherent orientations and three marked boundary arcs; a target plane with first two arcs on coordinate axes and third along the two outer sides s=h or t=h; generic interior z and oriented ray; indicate +/− crossing signs and cancellation on paired internal edges. Separately mark affine triangle coordinate bounds r and the area estimate if space permits.
candidate_diagrams.confidence: possible, source-supported; drawing must preserve noninjective/reversing affine maps and not imply a homeomorphism
